```{r setup, include=FALSE}
site <- identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = site,
                      message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
options(width = 100)
```

A two-part model fits whether the outcome is positive (the first part) and
the outcome among those with a positive value (the second part).
`suest_twopart()` combines the two parts, so predictions and marginal effects
are on the overall expected outcome, `Pr(y > 0) * E(y | y > 0)`, with
standard errors from the joint covariance matrix of the two parts.

The outcome is total medical expenditures of adults in the 2004 Medical
Expenditure Panel Survey; 18% had none. The first part is a logit for having
any expenditures; the second part is a Gamma model with a log link for the
amount among those with expenditures. Standard errors are clustered on the
dwelling unit, which family members share.

```{r fit}
library(suest)
library(marginaleffects)
library(haven)

meps <- zap_labels(read_dta("https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/meps.dta"))
meps[c("female", "ins_unins", "anylim")] <-
  lapply(meps[c("female", "ins_unins", "anylim")], factor)

any <- glm(I(exp_tot > 0) ~ age + female + lninc + pcs12 + mcs12 +
             ins_unins + anylim, family = binomial("logit"), data = meps)
amount <- glm(exp_tot ~ age + female + lninc + pcs12 + mcs12 + ins_unins +
                anylim, family = Gamma(link = "log"), data = meps,
              subset = exp_tot > 0)
fit <- suest_twopart(any, amount, model_names = c("Any", "Amount"),
                     cluster = "duid")
fit
```

For a Poisson pseudo-likelihood second part, use
`family = quasipoisson()` instead.

## Effects on expected expenditures

```{r effects}
avg_slopes(fit, variables = c("age", "female", "ins_unins", "anylim"))
```

## Effects in each part

`type = "prob"` gives the effects on the probability of any expenditures, and
`type = "conditional"` the effects on expenditures among those with any:

```{r parts}
avg_slopes(fit, variables = "ins_unins", type = "prob")
avg_slopes(fit, variables = "ins_unins", type = "conditional")
```

## Comparing groups

The effect of being uninsured for men (`female` 0) and women (`female` 1),
and the difference between them:

```{r groups}
by_sex <- avg_comparisons(fit, variables = "ins_unins", by = "female")
by_sex
hypotheses(by_sex, hypothesis = difference ~ pairwise)
```
